messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: unusual auth traffic detected against auth-proxy from 3 distinct IPs (sustained 401->200 pattern). Potential token replay or session-shadowing. Paging @sre-oncall @maria @kevin.

sre-oncall: I'm on call, looking at flow logs and proxy metrics now. any customer reports?

alex: quick check: seeing repeated session_id values across different tenant headers. sampling 1% of requests for full header dump. running: `jq '.session_id,.tenant' /tmp/auth-sample.json | sort | uniq -c`

maria: noted. If session_id reuse is real we should assume session signing key could be leaked or replayed. Recommend immediate rotation of the short-lived session signing secret + pause any non-essential log forwarding from staging.

kevin: standing up a canary with stricter token replay checks (nonce + token age). will patch auth-proxy config and deploy a canary in 5m.

cs-rep: two customers opened support tickets reporting 5xx around 09:12 UTC. not sure if related yet.

alex: correlating — the 5xx look like overloaded backend retries from our probe. No client-side error codes in samples yet.

maria: still seeing header fragments that include internal s3 paths in forwarded logs (staging). I'm pausing logshipper for staging now. `./scripts/disable-logshipper --env=staging`

infra-bot: logshipper(staging) pause requested by maria — job queued.

kevin: canary rolled with stricter checks. so far 0 errors; traffic routed 5% to canary. monitoring for false positives.

alex: WAF rule added to block the 3 suspicious IPs (45.72.11.3, 198.51.100.27, 203.0.113.9). applied at edge.

maria: starting rotation of the session signing key and rostering affected svc-keys for emergency rotation. I'll coordinate KMS key rotation steps and notify infra.

legal: hold on external notification until we confirm actual exfiltration. If logs contained customer-identifiable S3 paths that were forwarded externally, we may need to notify downstream vendors. Keep me posted.

cs-rep: flagged the two impacted customers and prepping an FYI template, awaiting legal signoff.

sre-oncall: mitigation summary so far: 1) WAF blocks applied 2) logshipper paused for staging 3) canary with stricter replay checks deployed 4) session signing key rotation initiated. No confirmed customer data exfiltration at this point.

maria: also enabling additional audit logging for all auth token issuance and refreshing retention to 90 days in case we need forensics.

alex: capturing a short pcap of auth-proxy egress for 10m window and exporting headers to secure bucket (access limited to sec and oncall). `tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/auth-egress.pcap port 443 and host auth-proxy`

kevin: will start a controlled restart of the log-collector on staging once logshipper pause completes to make sure no buffered forwards leak. ETA 8m.

legal: if you see any evidence of external exfiltration of customer data, escalate and we'll prepare notification. For now we treat as potential compromise.

cs-rep: customers informed that we're investigating with high priority; no customer-facing incident page yet until we confirm impact.

sre-oncall: handing off next steps to @alex for continued mitigation and to @maria for sec coordination. Handoff in ~2h; I'll stay available for escalations.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident severity updated P1 -> P2 (mitigations applied, active containment in progress).

maria: action items: finish key rotation, confirm no logs exported externally, coordinate legal/customer comms if exfiltration confirmed.

alex: action items: continue sampling, gather full request traces for the 09:00-09:20 UTC window, and start a brief post-incident runbook draft.

kevin: action items: verify canary behavior at 15% traffic if no false positives in 15m, then plan full rollout during low traffic window.

legal: I'll stand by to review any notification drafts.

cs-rep: thanks — keeping support tickets updated. will queue a proactive FYI draft if legal greenlights.

infra-bot: scheduled handoff reminder in 1h to @sre-noc.

sre-oncall: closing the live mitigation loop for now. Postmortem to be scheduled.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: containment stable, progress logged, postmortem required.
